An African writer and campaigner against the slave trade, who lived most of his life in Britain under the name Gustavus Vassa. By his own account he was born in Igbo country in what is now Nigeria, kidnapped as a boy and shipped across the Atlantic. Some historians think he may have been born in South Carolina; the question is open.

He was sold to a Royal Navy officer, then to a Quaker merchant in the West Indies, and bought his freedom in 1766. He worked at sea, travelled as far as the Arctic, and settled in London. He helped bring the Zong massacre to public notice and was a leader of the Sons of Africa, a group of Black abolitionists.

In 1789 he published The Interesting Narrative, his life story. It sold widely, went through many editions, and gave British readers a first-hand account of the Atlantic slave trade. He died ten years before Britain banned the trade.
